protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Verified. CanonicalUrl at the vulnerable tree strips a trailing .git before removing sparse+; SourceId::new then interns SourceIdInner values through a HashSet keyed by kind, precise, and CanonicalUrl. Thus sparse+https://host/index and sparse+https://host/index.git collapse to one inner identity and the second construction reuses the first raw URL, enabling credential reuse across distinct HTTPS paths.

The primary reaches the correct NOT_AI conclusion but inaccurately says outer SourceId equality and hashing directly use kind plus CanonicalUrl. At this revision, non-Git SourceId cmp/hash use the raw URL; the collision occurs earlier because SourceId::wrap interns SourceIdInner by kind, precise, and CanonicalUrl and reuses the first inner pointer/raw URL.

corrected_fields.bug_semantics: Cargo's CanonicalUrl unconditionally stripped a trailing .git, including from sparse registry URLs whose HTTPS paths are distinct. SourceId::new passed each sparse URL through CanonicalUrl and SourceId::wrap interned SourceIdInner in a HashSet whose equality/hash keys are kind, precise, and canonical_url. Consequently sparse+https://host/index and sparse+https://host/index.git retrieved the same interned inner value, including the first raw URL, so Cargo treated the attacker-controlled sibling registry as the credential-bearing registry. Outer non-Git SourceId cmp/hash themselves use the raw URL; the identity collapse is caused by SourceIdInner interning.
corrected_fields.evidence[7]: At 412b6339147265743488cb2fe6073cc250fdf7f0, SourceId::new computes CanonicalUrl and SourceId::wrap interns SourceIdInner through HashSet. SourceIdInner Hash/PartialEq use kind, precise, and canonical_url, while outer non-Git SourceId Hash/Ord use the raw URL after a pointer-equality fast path. The two sparse URLs therefore collide during interning and share one inner pointer/raw URL; they do not collide because outer SourceId directly hashes CanonicalUrl.
